chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, through his chain, raising it to 'Ali ibn Maymun al-Sa'igh, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

O 'Ali! It has reached me that some of our Shias allow one or two years to pass without visiting al-Husayn. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I know many people with this description.' He said, 'By Allah, they have missed their fortune, turned away from Allah's reward, and distanced themselves from the proximity of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, how often is the visit?' He said, 'O 'Ali, if you are able to visit him every month, do so.' I said, 'I cannot reach that because I work with my hands, people's affairs are in my hands, and I cannot absent my face from my place for even one day.' He said, 'You are excused, and whoever works with his hands. I meant those who do not work with their hands, for whom if they go out every Friday, it is easy for them. Indeed, they have no excuse with Allah and no excuse with His Messenger on the Day of Judgment.' I said, 'If a man sends someone on his behalf, is that permissible?' He said, 'Yes, and his going himself is greater in reward and better for him with his Lord. His Lord will see him sleepless at night, bearing the toil of the day. Allah will look at him with a glance that obliges for him the highest Firdaws with Muhammad and his family. So compete in that and be among its people.'

key_terms.أَعْمَلُ بِيَدِي: Manual laborer / working with one's hands

ai.seo_question: How often should one visit the shrine of Imam al-Husayn according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) distinguishes between the obligations of the wealthy and the working class, noting that while manual laborers are excused from frequent visits, those with leisure must not delay their ziyarah to Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). The hadith highlights the superior merit of personal pilgrimage over proxy visits, promising that God’s direct gaze upon the devotee secures entry into Al-Firdaws, thereby reinforcing the Shia emphasis on active, personal devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt as a means of spiritual proximity to the Prophet.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. My father narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, through his Isnād from ‘Ali ibn Maymūn Al-Sā`igh, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said to me, “O ‘Ali! I have heard that some of our Shia allow one or two years to pass without going to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)!” I replied, “May I sacrifice myself for you! I know many people who are like this.” Imam (a.s.) said, “I swear to Allāh that they have turned their backs to their own fortune, they have declined Allāh’s rewards, and they have distanced themselves from nearness to Muḥammad (s.a.a.w.).” I asked, “May I sacrifice myself for you! How often should one go to his Ziyārah?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “O ‘Ali! If you can go to his Ziyārah once every month, do so.” I said, “I cannot do that because I am a manual labourer; people’s affairs are pending in my hands and I cannot be absent from my work for even one day.” Imam (a.s.) replied: You are excused, as are other manual labourers. I was referring to people other than manual labourers, people who have the possibility of going (to the Ziyārah) every week. Such people will have no excuse in front of Allāh and His Messenger (s.a.a.w.) on the Day of Judgment (if they do not go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)). I asked, “Is it permissible for them to send someone on their behalf?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Yes. However, it is better for them and they will have a greater reward with their Lord if they go themselves, for He will see them sleepless at night and tired during the day (traveling to Ḥusain (a.s.)). Allāh will look at them with a glance which will inevitably cause them to dwell with Muḥammad (s.a.a.w.) and his family (a.s.) in the greatest places of Firdaws. Therefore, compete with one another in going (to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)) and be among those who adhere to it.
